paragraph:
Is it better to have 1 or 100 friends?
It is always better to have 1 friend than 100. It goes back to the age old saying ‘quality over quantity.’ One of the core principles of friendship is trust. Being able to truly and deeply understand and trust a person, and for them to trust you. Trust requires closeness, it requires that you spend time with them and that you experience the world with them. Physically, this type of trust is not feasible with 100 people. We are not wired to trust or truly know 100 people. We don’t have the time to cultivate deep and meaningful friendships with 100 people. 100 people is a lot of people. A room full of 100 people would be a full room. While some might say that 100 friends is ideal, giving you the opportunity to hear 100 different perspectives, learn about 100 different view points and experiences, how deep would these friendships truly be? Would they actually be friendships or would it just be 100 people who you are just slightly more than acquaintances with? 1 friend however, is much better. One friend to truly be your rock. One friend to truly listen to you. And one friend who truly knows you and you know them.
claim_clarity_justification: The claim that it is always better to have 1 friend than 100 is unambiguously stated at the beginning of the paragraph.
evidence_quality_justification: The argument provides specific conceptual reasons, defining friendship by trust and closeness and arguing for the infeasibility of this with 100 people due to human capacity and time constraints.
warrant_reasoning_justification: The logical connection between the definition of friendship (trust/closeness) and the impossibility of achieving it with 100 people due to time and human wiring is explicitly and soundly reasoned.
counterargument_justification: A specific counterargument regarding the benefit of 100 diverse perspectives is clearly acknowledged and effectively rebutted by questioning the depth of such relationships.
overall_persuasiveness_justification: The argument is very well-structured, flows logically from claim to support and counter-rebuttal, and builds to a convincing conclusion about the value of deep friendship.

It is crazy to state the billionaires should not exist, however, when you examine the facts, this claims starts to look less absurd. A billionaire dollars is an amount so obscene, no one could spend all their money in their lifetime even if they tried. Indeed, there is a psychological effect were billionaires believe they have everything and so much power and decide to do crazy things with it. Billionaires like Bryan Johnson who only goal is to live forever. He spends his days trying extreme things or having weird routines just to live longer his rich life. 

It’s not just about how you live your life, it how people can get that kind of money. There is no billionaire that is rich because they were just smart or ahead of the curve. Sure, it takes grit and many are talented people, but at it’s core to become that rich you either have to be born rich or exploit others. Only by exploiting others do your gains become so large. paragraph: It is honestly quite embarrassing that in 2026 the British Museum still holds onto the Parthenon Marbles. paragraph:

keeping them in London allows them to be seen in a global context alongside Egyptian or Assyrian art. Most artifacts aren't literally hacked off a standing unesco world heritage site like these were.

These aren’t just objects but they are part of a building that belongs to Athens.

paragraph:
Is the hippopotamus the best land mammal to win a fight? 
Hippos are the most dominant land mammal because their physical power and defensive capabilities far exceed those of any potential rival. Their huge size and surprising speed, make them one of worlds greatest beasts. Their biggest and most powerful advantage is their colossal jaws, one bite is strong enough to snap a canoe in half and powerful enough to crush bone with ease. This combined with their aggressive temperament, makes them uniquely equipped to defeat any predator which challenges them. Lions, crocodiles, and even groups of large mammals routinely yield to hippos, not out of caution but out of recognition that confronting them is a losing strategy. Their mass, speed, character, and bite, makes them a clear victor in any confrontation.

paragraph:
Is online learning better than in-person learning?

If you were to compare online learning with in person learning, you may finish with the same content understood, but the actual teaching and learning will be very different. Online learning can be considered better than in person learning regarding the teaching as it puts students in an environment where they have less distractions from friends and as a result, may be better able to focus on the content. Additionally, they have more time to digest the content and do further reading as the commute time is eliminated. Nevertheless, this may only be the case for more academically inclined students who enjoy studying. Those who dislike it may get more easily distracted in their bedrooms and decide not to participate in the classroom. Therefore, online learning may be better for learning for those who do well in school, but can be detrimental for those who have a strong hatred against it leading to high procrastination.
claim_clarity_justification: The main claim is clearly stated at the end of the paragraph, though it evolves from an initial question and qualified throughout.
evidence_quality_justification: The argument provides specific and relevant support, such as less distractions from friends and elimination of commute time, to back its points.
warrant_reasoning_justification: The logical connections between the benefits of online learning and the eventual qualified claim are explicit and easy to follow.
counterargument_justification: The paragraph acknowledges a specific counterargument regarding students who are not academically inclined and integrates it into the final nuanced claim.
overall_persuasiveness_justification: The argument is well-structured, flows logically, effectively incorporates a counterargument, and presents a convincing, nuanced conclusion.

paragraph:
Is there any merit to the US’s ambitions over Greenland?
I believe the United States’s ambitions to take over Greenland are still internationally unjustified since it is a sovereign nation and part of NATO. That being said, if you argue from the point of view of American interests alone, it is possible to see long-term economic and geopolitical benefits for them, assuming they manage to maintain their relationship with NATO countries through a purchase deal or a referendum vote of Greenland,d where they choose to join the US and leave the Kingdom of Denmark. Furthermore, if the US invests in the people of Greenland, develops its infrastructure, and maintains NATO security for all allied members, that can justify the US’s ambitions in Greenland.

paragraph:
Is there any merit to the US’s ambitions over Greenland?
Greenland’s location in the Arctic is clearly important in geopolitics, as it lies between the US and Russia and is a frozen, underdeveloped land where missiles and military bases can be stationed. The US claims that having control over Greenland is essential to US national security. While I agree that Greenland is strategic to US ambitions, I strongly oppose the US's ambitions to unite Greenland with the US. Firstly, Greenland, part of the Kingdom of Denmark, is a part of NATO and a close ally of the US. They already allow the US to operate military bases. In fact, the US has reduced its presence in the Arctic over the years and can still reinstall its bases. Furthermore, while US national security is important to the US, aggression against a sovereign nation and a close ally, part of the strongest military alliance to ever exist, threatens international stability and US strength. Secondly, the claim is that if the US does not take control of Greenland, China's presence in the Arctic will be mostly baseless, since China’s presence in the Arctic was completely removed during the first Trump administration. Overall, my claim is that the US’s aggressive ambitions over Greenland are purely territorial and driven by Trump’s ego rather than by national security.
claim_clarity_justification: The core position opposing US ambitions over Greenland and attributing them to ego rather than national security is clearly and specifically articulated.
evidence_quality_justification: The paragraph provides several relevant points, including existing military agreements and a specific rebuttal to the "China threat" argument, though some points could be further developed.
warrant_reasoning_justification: The logical connections between the provided evidence (existing alliances, China's removed presence) and the negation of national security as a driver for US ambitions are clear, though the direct leap to "Trump's ego" is more of an assertion.
counterargument_justification: The paragraph explicitly acknowledges the US national security justification and the concern about China's presence, then effectively rebuts both with specific counterpoints.
overall_persuasiveness_justification: The argument is well-structured and follows a logical progression of acknowledging, claiming, and providing support, making it mostly convincing despite the inferential leap to "Trump's ego."

This is believed to be because the HPA axis becomes dysregulated and there is a constant high level of cortisol being released by the adrenal glands. This glucocorticoids travels through the blood to then act in most cells of the body through its receptor (GR) is thought when in high concentrations for long to have detrimental effects on the brain. The hippocampus specifically has a huge concentration of GR is thought to be very vulnerable; usually it has a negative feedback role on the HPA axis but in chronically stressed people is thought to not do this anymore. Many antidepressant drugs that change neurotransmitter levels in the brain actually take a long time to reduce depressive szptoms even if the neurotransmitter ells are changed almost immediately, for this reason isìt is thought to be some other mechanism downstream; scientists have shown that many of these adnitdperessants actually activated the BDNF receptor leading to neurogenesis; specidfically in the hippocampus ; and therefore that is this mechainsism that teals to better regulation of the HPA axis and so recovers od depressive symptoms.

evidence_quality_justification: The author provides multiple specific biological components, such as the HPA axis, glucocorticoid receptors, and BDNF, to support the argument.

paragraph:
Is adult hippocampal neurogenesis necessary to recover from stressed induced depression?
Chronic stress dysregulates the HPA axis, leading to persstent cortisol release that damages the hippocampus, a region vital for stress regulation via its high density of glucocorticoid receptors. 

The neurogenesis hypothesis explains the delayed effiacy of antidepressants: while neurotransmitter levels change quickly, clinical recovery likely requires downstream BDNF activation to generate new hippocampal neurons.The neurogenesis hypothesis helps explain why antidepressants, often take weeks to improve a patient mood. This delay suggests a downstream mechanism: many antidepressants activate BDNF receptors, which trigger adult hippocampal neurogenesis. However, the necessity of neurogenesis remains a point of debate. Counter-evidence suggests that some patients show recovery through synaptic plasticity rather than the birth of new neurons. Furthermore, animal studies have shown that blocking neurogenesis doesn't always prevent antidepressants from working in every behavioral test. Therefore, while hippocampal neurogenesis is a primary driver of recovery, it may be part of a broader network of structural repairs required to reverse stress-induced depression.
claim_clarity_justification: The author concludes with a clear, nuanced position that neurogenesis is a primary driver of recovery but functions as part of a broader structural network.
evidence_quality_justification: The argument incorporates specific biological mechanisms including BDNF activation, HPA axis regulation, and results from animal behavioral tests.
warrant_reasoning_justification: The logical link between the clinical delay of antidepressant efficacy and the time required for neurogenesis is explicitly and soundly established.
counterargument_justification: The paragraph acknowledges and meaningfully integrates conflicting evidence regarding synaptic plasticity and neurogenesis-independent recovery in animal studies.
overall_persuasiveness_justification: The paragraph is highly coherent and builds a convincing case by balancing technical mechanisms with acknowledged scientific counter-evidence.
